image_description: A full-body side view of a chestnut/sorrel horse standing in a grassy field with trees in the background. The horse has a reddish-brown coat, a flaxen mane and tail, and white markings (socks) on its lower legs. It is wearing a blue halter.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elongated head with large expressive eyes and mobile ears.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head profile is clearly visible, showing an elongated shape, distinct eye, and upright ear. Anatomically correct.
The neck shows a natural crest and muscle definition consistent with equine anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Athletic build with tall, lean proportions at the withers.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The horse displays a standard athletic conformation with a defined wither area.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Uniform brownish-orange to light chestnut coat coloration with no black points.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The checkpoint requires a 'uniform' coat. The image clearly shows white socks on the lower legs, which violates the strict definition of 'uniform' coloration provided in the taxonomy, even though the base coat is correct sorrel/chestnut.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Mane and tail same color as body or lighter (flaxen).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mane and tail are visibly lighter (flaxen/blonde) than the reddish body coat, which is characteristic of sorrel/chestnut horses.
The torso depth and topline appear structurally sound and anatomically correct.
The tail is long, attached correctly, and shows individual hair strands.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Long slender legs with single hoof per foot.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: All four legs are visible. They are slender and end in single hooves. No extra limbs or fusion detected.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The transition between the white socks and the hooves is slightly soft/painterly compared to the sharpness of the body coat. The hooves lack some fine surface detail texture.

The blue halter straps blend into the fur at the connection points near the noseband, lacking crisp edge definition. This suggests minor structural fusion rather than just optical blur, warranting a higher severity rating.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific breed/color classification (Sorrel/Chestnut) and rule out misclassification as a generic horse or other equine.
To verify the structural integrity of the four legs and ensure no hidden limb fusion or anatomical impossibilities in the stance.
To specifically audit the boundary between the blue halter and the horse's head to determine if the observed blending is artifact fusion or acceptable depth-of-field blur.
To assess overall image coherence, lighting consistency, and detect any subtle generative noise or blur.

focus_areas: Coat color uniformity vs. white markings (strict taxonomy check)
Boundary integrity of halter straps against fur
Edge sharpness of mane and tail against background
